subject: Atlas Health - latency exception request & operational playbook
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Coleman <jordan.coleman@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Atlas Health - request for tighter latency commitment
Attachments: atlas_request_summary.pdf

Tessa / Karthik,

Quick context: Atlas Health (large strategic prospect) is pushing for a narrower latency commitment for their clinical inference flows. They want a written amendment to our standard SLA for a p95 <= 80ms for their production traffic (real-time triage endpoint) and 99.99% availability on the dedicated endpoint. Procurement says this is a gating item for the deal timeline.

Key asks from Atlas (attached summary):
- p95 <= 80ms for their dedicated endpoint (steady-state, not cold-start)
- 99.99% monthly uptime for that endpoint
- A canary rollout and 30-day pilot before full ramp
- On-call escalation: 24/7 pager with runbook and fortnightly ops reviews

We need a cross-functional feasibility note and a proposed approval path (product constraints, estimated cost delta for Dedicated capacity, required monitoring/runbook, and legal/procurement handoffs). Can you review and flag blockers?

Jordan from Atlas is on-copy — hoping to keep this high-velocity.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Atlas Health - request for tighter latency commitment

Thanks Monica — looping in Product and Eng for a quick read.

Summary for the group: Atlas requests an exception to our standard public SLA tied to a dedicated endpoint. They expect sub-80ms p95 and 99.99% availability. They plan to start with a 30-day pilot/canary.

Ask of Product (Karthik): what can we promise in writing? Is a staged/conditional commitment acceptable (e.g., pilot -> limited SLA -> full SLA after metrics)? What operational guarantees and measurement definitions do we need (endpoint definition, traffic shape, synthetic checks vs. real traffic, maintenance windows)?

Ask of Eng (Hiro): initial feasibility and a quick estimate of the infra levers required (dedicated pool size, autoscale headroom, KV/prefix caching, quantization expectations). High-level cost delta and any changes needed to our monitoring and alerting to support a contractual SLO.

I'll gather legal and CS once we have a technical + product stance. Jordan — we'll aim to get you a proposal by EOD Tuesday.

—Tessa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Atlas Health - request for tighter latency commitment (technical assessment)
Attachments: benchmark_80ms_run-20250511.csv

High-level technical read (TL;DR: feasible with constraints + cost):

What makes p95 <= 80ms hard:
- model size and sequence length: their payloads average 1.2k tokens which increases decode time
- multi-tenant noise: bursty traffic can increase queueing if shared pool used

Options to meet the ask:
1) Dedicated GPU pool pinned to Atlas model/variant + explicit throughput reservation. This gives us control over queueing and predictable scheduler latency.
2) Aggressive KV/prefix caching for common prefixes (they have predictable request patterns). This reduces per-request compute.
3) Quantized model runtime (int8/4) with validation on accuracy for their payloads — needs eval but big perf win.
4) Limit SLA to specific endpoint(s) (real-time triage) and exclude large-batch or admin routes.

Operational asks:
- Canary pilot with traffic ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 30 days, with close monitoring of p95 and tail latencies.
- Dedicated metrics dashboard (token-level latency, queue depth, GPU utilization) and a runbook for evictions/fallbacks.
- Automatic fallback to a slightly higher-latency compatible model variant if thermal or capacity events are detected.

Estimated incremental cost (very rough):
- Baseline Dedicated pool (g4dn-style equivalent): additional ~$35k/month for reserved capacity to hit sub-80ms at current traffic profile.
- Monitoring/Runbook/On-call: ~$6k/month operational overhead (eng+SRE rotation).
- One-time engineering effort for canary automation and synthetic checks: 2-3 engineer-weeks.

Constraints / risks:
- 99.99% monthly availability at p95 implies only ~4.3 minutes of monthly downtime. Meeting that end-to-end requires coordination with infra cloud provider availability windows and backup endpoints.
- If we allow their traffic to grow >X (TBD), the cost and schedule must be revisited.

If Product wants to proceed, I recommend we require a dedicated pool + staged SLA and include failure modes and automatic fallbacks in the contract. Attaching quick benchmark CSV showing p95 numbers from a small internal run (see attachment).

—Hiro
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-05-12T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Atlas Health - request for tighter latency commitment (proposal + next steps)
Attachments: proposed-runbook-v1.pdf

Thanks all for the fast turnaround — consolidating Product position and proposed approval path.

Product position (concise):
- We can offer a conditional SLA exception for Atlas provided the following are contractually agreed:
  1) Dedicated endpoint scoped to "triage-realtime" traffic only (explicit path and API keys).
  2) Staged commitment: pilot (30 days, canary traffic ramp) -> limited SLA (first 3 months) -> full SLA after metrics validation.
  3) Explicit exclusion list (large-batch, export endpoints, non-critical admin traffic).
  4) Fallback policy: automated switch to a compatible model variant with documented degradation & notification cadence.

Operational requirements we need in contract:
- Reserved capacity sizing clause and billing delta (per Hiro's estimate).
- Rights to run synthetic checks and schedule maintenance with 72h notice.
- Joint on-call rotation expectations and monthly ops review for first 6 months.

Approval path recommendation:
1) Product + Eng sign-off on proposed-runbook-v1.pdf (attached).
2) Finance approval of committed reserved capacity pricing (Monica to own).
3) Legal to draft an SLA amendment with the staged commitment language (we'll supply failure modes and measurement definitions).
4) Exec sign-off (Director-level) for any SLA promises that materially change standard terms (>X cost delta).

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Eng (Hiro): finalize canary automation + final cost numbers by 2025-05-16.
- Sales (Monica): confirm Atlas accepts staged commitment and cost delta by 2025-05-14.
- Product (Karthik): deliver measurement spec and draft amendment language by 2025-05-15.
- Tessa: coordinate Legal & CS once numbers are in.

Jordan — cc'd — let us know if the staged approach and dedicated endpoint boundary are acceptable; we will pause formal drafting until Atlas confirms.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
